issue_context.title: HTTP2: Reuse request and response Pipe
issue_context.body:
Allocations related to request and response pipes are a top cause of allocations:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/303201/75140250-61076c80-5753-11ea-8f28-7707290163b6.png)

Making the Http2OutputProducer at the same time would be a good idea.

review_comments: I'm actually surprised that ConcurrentPipeWriter doesn't show up in your profile. I guess there aren't many scenarios where it would allocate.
For comparison, how much did it allocate before?
@halter73 wanted to check these values before reusing a stream. HasResponseCompleted ensures the output producer task has been awaited
Why would we return the stream before then?

If an app didn't await a write, and Kestrel didn't try to flush a suffix.

Not very likely, but you could imagine some app doing some custom Task.WhenAny/Task.Delay logic on a response body write, and then throwing if the delay finishes before the write. Of course the app *should* just use a cancellation token, but I don't see the harm in guarding against this.
This should throw if it's not completed.

How do we know if the ConcurrentPipeWriter has been completed or not?

The underlying pipe will always be reset along side this type when the stream is reset, so it will throw when not complete, but not from this method.

> How do we know if the ConcurrentPipeWriter has been completed or not?

For one, `_completeException` should not be null. And it should be nulled out in reset. Additionally, everything that is nulled/zeroed out should already be nulled/zeroed out if the ConcurrentPipeWriter was completed.

Another thing to be aware of is that the ConcurrentPipeWriter is responsible for completing the inner PipeWriter. Nothing else should be completing the inner PipeWriter.

And if there's a pending flush at the time the ConcurrentPipeWriter is Completed, ConcurrentPipeWriter.Complete() will set the the `_completeException` to a non-null value and return immediately before completing the inner PipeWriter. ConcurrentPipeWriter will then complete the inner PipeWriter later after all the data is flushed through the inner PipeWriter.

Currently the only way to observe that a ConcurrentPipeWriter is done from the outside is to flush it after the app exits, wait for the flush task to complete, *then* call ConcurrentPipeWriter.Complete().

_currentFlushTcs, _bufferedWritePending and _aborted would also need to be reset.
Not sure this is worth pooling. If we do pool, _pendingUpdateSize and _windowUpdatesDisabled should be reset.
I'm very aware. I was referring to InputFlowControl.cs.
Ah ok. Now resetting those variables.

I'm concerned about pooling the StreamOutputFlowControl here. Couldn't the client update the InitialWindowSize for the connection and the stream wouldn't get the updated size as it wouldn't be updated on Reset? @Tratcher thoughts as well. I think _outputFlowControl should take an int for the InitialWindowSize for reset.

Yeah, context.ClientPeerSettings.InitialWindowSize needs to be checked at the start of each new stream because it may have changed in between. That might just mean you need to pass the value into Reset.
